# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉]

I see the bomb clearly. It has a white display and three wires: green, blue, and red (left to right). I cannot hear or touch, but I can speak to Mute and Blind, and gesture to Mute.

Blind just gestured `[👋 👉]` at me. Since I am Deaf, I *see* these gestures.
- `👋` usually means "Hello" or "Stop/Wait".
- `👉` points right.

This is ambiguous. Did Blind point to the red wire (rightmost)? Or did they mean something else? I need to establish communication with Mute first, as Mute has the manual. Mute can see my gestures and hear my speech. Blind can hear my speech but not see my gestures (since I'm not sure if Blind can see gestures—wait, the rules say "Whoever can see receives it". Blind cannot see. So Blind only hears my speech. Mute can see my gestures and hear my speech.)

My goal: Get Mute to tell us what the manual says about this specific configuration (White Display, 3 Wires).

Plan:
1. Speak to everyone (Mute and Blind) to describe the bomb's visual state precisely.
2. Gesture to Mute to ask for help/confirmation.

Let's start by describing the bomb to Mute via speech, since Mute can hear. Then I will gesture to Mute to point out the wires.

Actually, simpler: Just speak the description. Mute can read the manual based on that.

Description: "Display is white. Three wires from left to right: Green, Blue, Red."

I will also gesture to Mute to ensure they are paying attention or to indicate the wires if possible, but text is safer for complex info. Let's stick to speech for the data.

To Mute: "The bomb has a white display. There are three wires. Left is green, middle is blue, right is red."

I should also acknowledge Blind's gesture if possible, but I don't know what it meant yet. Better to focus on getting the manual info.

```
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb has a white display. There are three wires. Left is green, middle is blue, right is red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"]) 
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟]

I see the bomb has changed. The display is still 0, but the light is now yellow (was white). The wires are Green (1), Red (2), Blue (3).
Mute gestured "✋" (Stop/Wait) to me. This suggests Mute might be confused or wants me to hold on, possibly because my previous description didn't match what they saw in the manual for a *white* light, or perhaps they are processing. However, the state has clearly changed.
Blind gestured "👉 🤟". 👉 points right (to the blue wire?), and 🤟 is "I love you" or "Rock on", often used as a generic "OK" or "Here" in ad-hoc sign languages if not defined. Or maybe it's just noise.

Crucially, the bomb state is dynamic. I must report the *current* state immediately so Mute can look up the correct rule. The previous state (White light) is gone.

I will speak the new configuration to everyone (Mute and Blind) so Mute can consult the manual for "Yellow Light, Display 0, Wires: Green, Red, Blue".

```
speak(to="mute", text="State change! Light is now YELLOW. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now YELLOW. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉]

The bomb state has changed again. The light is now orange (previously yellow, before that white). The wires remain Green (1), Red (2), Blue (3). The display remains 0.

Mute gestured "👉" (point right) to me. This likely refers to the rightmost wire, which is Blue. However, without knowing the rule for an Orange Light with Display 0, I cannot confirm if cutting the blue wire is correct or safe. Mute might be indicating that the manual says something about the rightmost wire, or they are just echoing Blind's previous gesture.

I must report the current visual state to Mute immediately so they can look up the specific rule for "Orange Light, Display 0". My previous message described a Yellow light, which is no longer valid.

I will speak the new configuration to both Mute and Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now ORANGE. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now ORANGE. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👉]

The light has changed to purple. The wires remain Green, Red, Blue (left to right). Display is 0.
Mute gestured "👍 👉". This likely means "Good/Correct" and "Point Right". Since the rightmost wire is Blue, Mute might be indicating that the Blue wire is the one to cut, or perhaps pointing out the last wire in a sequence. However, I need to be sure about the rule for Purple Light + Display 0.

I will report the current state (Purple) to Mute and Blind. If Mute's previous gesture was based on the Orange state, it might be obsolete now. But if they are signaling a general rule or confirming a specific wire, I should listen. Given the rapid changes, I must keep them updated.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now PURPLE. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now PURPLE. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉]

The bomb state has changed again. The light is now **red**. The display remains **0**. The wires remain **Green (1), Red (2), Blue (3)**.

Mute gestured `✋ 👉` to me.
- `✋` means "Stop" or "Wait".
- `👉` points Right.

This combination suggests Mute wants us to wait, but is also pointing towards the right side of the bomb (the Blue wire). It is possible that for a Red Light with Display 0, the rule involves the rightmost wire, or perhaps Mute is signaling that we should *not* act yet despite the point. Given the previous rapid changes and the explicit "Stop" gesture, I must not assume cutting is safe. I need to confirm the exact manual instruction for this specific configuration: **Red Light, Display 0**.

I will speak the current state clearly to both Mute and Blind so they can verify the rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is RED. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is RED. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉]

The bomb state has reverted to the initial configuration: **White Light**, Display **0**, Wires **Green, Red, Blue**.

Mute is gesturing `✋ 👉` again.
- `✋` (Stop/Wait) suggests that acting on this state might be incorrect or premature based on their manual lookup, or perhaps they are warning us not to cut yet because the state is cycling.
- `👉` (Point Right) points to the Blue wire (Wire 3).

Since the light changed from Red back to White, and Mute's gesture remained consistent (`✋ 👉`) for both Red and White states (though the previous turn was Red, now it is White), I need to clarify if the rule depends on the color specifically. In Turn 4 (Purple), Mute gestured `👍 👉`. In Turn 5 (Red), Mute gestured `✋ 👉`. Now in Turn 6 (White), Mute gestures `✋ 👉`.

This implies:
- Purple + Display 0 -> "Good" + Point Right (Cut Blue?)
- Red + Display 0 -> "Stop" + Point Right
- White + Display 0 -> "Stop" + Point Right

If "Stop" means "Do Not Cut", then we should not cut the blue wire when the light is White or Red. If "Stop" just means "Wait for next state", we are in a loop. However, usually "Stop" in these puzzles means "Don't do that action".

I must report the current visual state (White) to ensure Mute knows we are looking at the same thing. I will also ask for clarification on what to do with the wires given the "Stop" signal. Since `❓` is not a valid gesture symbol, I will use speech to ask Mute directly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is WHITE. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE. You signaled STOP and POINT RIGHT. Does this mean do NOT cut the blue wire?")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is WHITE. Display is 0. Wires left-to-right: GREEN, RED, BLUE.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👉]

The bomb state has changed to **Yellow Light**, Display **0**, Wires **Green, Red, Blue**.

Mute gestured `👍 👉` (Thumbs Up + Point Right).
- In Turn 4 (Purple), Mute also gestured `👍 👉`.
- In Turns 5 and 6 (Red/White), Mute gestured `✋ 👉` (Stop + Point Right).

This pattern suggests that for **Yellow** and **Purple** lights with Display 0, the "Point Right" (Blue wire) is confirmed as the correct action ("Thumbs Up"). For **Red** and **White** lights, it is not ("Stop").

Since the light is now Yellow, and Mute confirms "Good" + "Right", I should signal Blind to cut the rightmost wire (Blue). Blind cannot see gestures, so I must speak the instruction clearly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is YELLOW. Cut the BLUE wire (rightmost, #3).")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirming: Yellow Light, Cut Blue Wire?")
```
